text:
maria: Quick flag — after converting rerank-v3 to int8 we see ndcg@5 drop ~2.8% and ndcg@10 ~2.1% on the news-rerank_v1 harvest. suspect text artifacts in candidates. asking for quick triage.
leo: numbers? sample size?
maria: 15k validation queries. fp16: ndcg@5=0.421, ndcg@10=0.472, mrr=0.339. int8-ptq: ndcg@5=0.409, ndcg@10=0.462, mrr=0.333. same eval harness, same candidate files.
priya: interesting. did the quant toolchain change tokenization or do anything to tokenizer files?
maria: no tokenizer swap. did a straight PTQ using our usual calibration set. delta persists across seeds.
dan: could be candidate ordering or padding boundaries interacting with KV packing. have you profiled the per-request sequence lengths?
maria: I dumped seqlen histograms: int8 eval showed slightly higher median batch-seqlen due to some long markdown snippets with tables. fp16 run used a preprocess that collapsed some whitespace — i realized we forgot that step for int8 run.
leo: aha. markdown tables and inline code can blow up subtokens. that affects batching and attention kernels.
priya: try normalizing candidates by removing markdown/code fences and collapsing multi-space. also check for BOMs and zero-width chars.
maria: ran a quick trial: cleaned candidates -> int8 ndcg@5=0.418, ndcg@10=0.471, mrr=0.337. almost back to fp16.
dan: that suggests the gap is mostly due to preproc mismatch rather than quant per se. still want to rerun larger sample to be sure.
leo: add an eval that preserves raw candidates too so we can monitor production differences. also note in rerank onboarding that canonicalization must be identical between formats.
priya: can you paste the exact eval commands so we can reproduce?
maria: sure:
```
python -m eval.rerank --model rerank-v3-fp16 --queries v1_val_15k.jsonl --candidates news_candidates_v1.jsonl --metrics ndcg@5,ndcg@10,mrr --seed 11
python -m eval.rerank --model rerank-v3-int8 --queries v1_val_15k.jsonl --candidates news_candidates_v1.cleaned.jsonl --metrics ndcg@5,ndcg@10,mrr --seed 11
```
(eval-bot): job 52240 finished: fp16 -> ndcg@5=0.421 ndcg@10=0.472 mrr=0.339; int8 (uncleaned) -> ndcg@5=0.409 ndcg@10=0.462 mrr=0.333
maria: follow-ups — 1) I'll run 50k sample AB with both cleaned and raw pipelines 2) add a unit test in preproc that flags candidate files containing markdown tables/code > 100 tokens 3) update bring-up checklist to include "candidate canonicalization parity".
leo: for the unit test, maybe just compute token-count delta before/after strip and fail if delta>10% for >1% of docs, to avoid noisy failures.
dan: also check inference batching config: int8 runtime did a different micro-batch packing in our staging cluster yesterday. verify runtime configs are matched for the AB.
priya: thanks — this is a good example of text-surface causing apparent model regressions. document it in the reranker onboarding notes.
maria: logging the gist with the clean script: https://internal.gist/clean-news-candidates.py. will post results when the 50k jobs finish.
eval-bot: job 52272 queued: int8 + cleaned candidates 50k run (seeds 11,77), ETA ~1h 45m
